title: How to Handle Stakeholder Pushback (Without Caving)
description:
When a stakeholder pushes back hard on your roadmap call, the answer isn't to win the argument or cave on the spot -- it's a specific four-step move. This Short walks through handling disagreement from stakeholders, using a real sales-vs-SSO example straight from the lesson.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/product-manager-mastery-path/level-1/09-stakeholder-communication-basics/

#Shorts

beats.narration: A sales lead is furious. Your roadmap put 'Enterprise readiness' in Next, not Now -- they swear a deal needs SSO to close. Cave, or dig in?
The move isn't winning the argument or caving on the spot. First, restate their concern back to them, so they know you actually heard it.

display.heading: Restate Their Concern First
display.subheading: Confirm you understood it, in your own words.

beats.narration: Next, share the reasoning behind the call, and ask what would actually change your mind -- new data, a bigger deal, a constraint you didn't know.

display.heading: Share Reasoning, Then Ask
display.subheading: What would actually change your mind?

beats.narration: In the real example, the PM asked exactly that, then got the deal size and close date instead of re-prioritizing on the spot.

display.heading: The Real Move
display.subheading: "So this deal is blocked without SSO -- is that right?"

beats.narration: If it's still unresolved, escalate it openly instead of letting it quietly fester -- and always follow up in writing within 48 hours.

display.heading: Still Unresolved? Escalate Transparently
display.subheading: Loop in whoever has the final call -- both sides represented fairly.

beats.narration: That's how you handle stakeholder disagreement without losing trust. Full breakdown's linked below.
